Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS : 4266 1967 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
LOCKERS, BEDSIDE FOR HOSPITAL USE 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 21 September 1967, after the draft finalized by the 
Hospital Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Consumer Products Division Council. 

0.2 The formulation of Indian Standards on hospital equipment has 
been taken up at the instance of the Advisory Committee for 
Development of Medical Instruments, Equipment and Appliances of 
the Government of India. 

0.3 This standard forms one of a series of Indian Standards on hospital 
furniture. Other standards in the series are as follows: 

IS : 4033-1968 General requirements for hospital furniture 

IS : 4034-1968 Specification for castors for hospital equipment 

IS : 4035-1967 Specification for trolleys, stretcher 

IS : 4036-1967 Specification for trolleys, patient 

IS : 4037-1967 Specification for stretcher and stretcher carriers 

IS : 4267-1967 Specification for stand, wash hand basin 

0.4 In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from the 
following: 

B.S. 1765 : 1951 Hospital bedside lockers. British Standards 
Institution. 

AA-C-lOa Cabinet, bedside, metal, hospital type. U.S. Federal 
Supply Service, USA. 

0.5 In some of the clauses of the standard, reference has been made to 
IS : 4033-1968 General requirements for hospital furniture* and 
IS : 4034-1968 Specification for castors for hospital equipment' which 
are under preparation. Until these standards are published, the 
requirements in such clauses shall be subject to agreement between 
the concerned parties. 

0.6 This edition 1.3 incorporates Amendment No. 3 (May 1993). Side 
bar indicates modification of the text as the result of incorporation of 
the amendment. Amendment Nos. 1 & 2 had been incorporated earlier. 



IS : 4266 1967 

0.7 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 
this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 
expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS : 21960*. The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the 
specified value in this standard. 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays down requirements of bedside lockers used in 
hospitals and other similar institutions. 

2. MATERIALS 

2.1 Frame Work -- shall be according to 2.1 of IS : 4033 1968t. 

2.2 Top — shall be according to 2.2 (a) and 2.2 (b) of IS : 4033 1968t. 

2.3 Cabinet Body — shall be according to 2.2 (a) of IS : 4033-19681. 

3. DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The main dimensions of the locker shall be as given in Fig. I. 

3.2 The thickness of tube used for the legs of the locker and the 
corresponding outside diameter shall be as given below: 

a) Thickness of tube 1.20 mm 

b) Outside diameter of tube 22.22 mm 

3.2.1 The legs of the locker may also be made of square tubes of 25 mm 
side and 1.2 mm thickness. 

3.3 The minimum thickness of metal sheets used for top and cabinet 
body shall be 1 .0 mm. If the top is superimposed by stainless steel sheet 
then the minimum thickness of stainless steel sheet shall be 0.5 mm. 

4. MANUFACTURE 

4.1 Top — The top shall be formed by pressing or bending the edges 
and welding the corners and it shall be welded neatly to the legs. The 
mild steel top may be superimposed by stainless steel sheet having a 
minimum thickness of 0.5 mm. 

4.2 Legs — Legs of the locker shall be welded to the top and the locker 
cabinet but prior to welding these shall be adjusted in a perfect upright 
position. Welding shall fully penetrate and there shall not be any 
sharp edges and unsealed formations. At the floor end of legs rubber or 
nylon shoes shall be provided. 

* Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised).

IS : 4266 - 1967 

4.3 Cabinet 

4.3.1 Sides and Back — The aides and back of the cabinet shall be 
made in one piece. Top and bottom shall be welded to it. The cabinet 
top may be superimposed with stainless steel sheet of 0.5 mm 
minimum thickness, if required by the purchaser. 

4.3.2 Door — Door of the cabinet shall be made by welding a 1.25 mm 
thick mild steel wsheet. The door shall work on pivot hinges and shall be 
flush with the front of the cabinet. The hinges shall be entirely 
concealed and hung to swing the door to a maximum of 120**. One leaf 
of the hinge shall be welded to the body of the cabinet and the other 
end shall be preferably spot welded to the cabinet door. 

4.3.3 Latch — It shall be door-knob operated latch and it shall operate 
smoothly. 

4.3.4 Louvers — The door of the cabinet shall be provided with a set of 
three ventilating louvers without shutters, having openings facing 
downward. The opening shall be approximately 75 mm long, 20 mm 
wide and 8 mm from the surface. 

5. FINISH 

5.1 The finish shall be according to 5 of IS : 4033-1968*. 

5.2 The door-knob shall be chromium plated over nickel with a smooth 
shining finish. 

6. TESTS 

6.0 The locker shall withstand the drop test as described in 6.1. 

6.1 Drop Test — The locker shall be held loosely by hooking it at the 
top portion of the leg and lifted in such a manner that the lowest point 
of the locker is 150 mm from the floor. It shall then be allowed to drop 
on to the floor without toppling. This shall be repeated on the other 
legs. After completion of the test, there shall be no distortion or 
opening of any welded joint. 

7. MARKING 

7.1 The marking shall be in accordance with 7 of IS : 4033-1968*. 

8. PACKING 

8.1 The packing shall be as specified in 8 of IS : 4033-1968*. 



^General requirements for hospital furniture.

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory iastitution estfiblished under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harrnotiious development of the activities of standardization, marl^ing and ({uality certification of 
goods and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any 
form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use. in the course 
of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade 
designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the necKl arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also 
reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments Is realTirmed when such review Indicates 
that no changes are needed: If the review indicates that changes are needed. It is taken up for 
revision. Usei"s of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest 
amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of BIS Catalogue' and 'Standards : Monthly 
Additions'.
